title: Frequently Asked Questions about White Sharks — AWSC
text: Frequently Asked Questions Do you have more questions?  We have answers.  Click below to find out answers to our most frequently asked questions, or contact us below. Image by Pam King White Sharks off Cape Cod Has there been a rise in the number of white sharks off Cape Cod? + Yes. Over the past decade, Cape Cod has emerged as a 'hot spot' in the northwest Atlantic where white sharks aggregate. Many modern-day residents and visitors of Cape Cod believe that recent increases in the regional abundance of white sharks is a new development. However, though records of white sharks are relatively sparse, archeological evidence, available catch data and anecdotal accounts suggest the 400-million-year-old species has a long history in the region. What is driving the surge in sharks? The abundance of white sharks in the area has increased over the past decade primarily in response to the local population recovery of gray seals, a favored food source for white sharks. Gray seals have recolonized the region following the prohibition of bounty hunting by the state of Massachusetts in the 1960s and the passage of the Marine Mammal Protection Act in 1972. What is the role of sharks in the marine environment? + White sharks are apex predators and as such are a critical species in the maintenance of a healthy and balanced marine environment. How many white sharks are in the waters along the coast of Cape Cod?  + While we don’t have an exact current figure, the results of our study, An open spatial capture−recapture framework for estimating the abundance and seasonal dynamics of white sharks at aggregation sites, estimated that approximately 800 individual white sharks visited the waters off Cape Cod between 2015 and 2018. Are the sharks changing their behavior hunting closer to shore or becoming more aggressive? + There is no evidence of that. Hunting for seals in shallow water close to shore hasn’t changed since white sharks started predictably showing up to feed on seals in the summer and the fall. Do sharks only eat seals? + No. White sharks are opportunistic predators. While seals are a particularly good meal and one of the favorite foods of an adult white shark, sharks also eat fish, squid, and other sharks. What a shark eats is also related to its size. The teeth of white sharks change as they get older. When they are young and under 10 feet, white shark teeth are pointed and less serrated, which is better for grasping slippery prey items such as fish and squid. When they grow to be over 10 feet and broaden out, their teeth become more serrated, which better equips them for eating seals. Image by Cody DeGroff Human Encounters with Atlantic White Sharks Do white sharks prey on people? + White sharks aren’t out to get you. People are not on a shark’s menu. If they were, the number of encounters between sharks and people would be much higher. When bites do occur, our research indicates it was likely triggered for one of three reasons: Mistaken identity. Sharks can misperceive a person as a marine mammal. Curiosity. Sharks use their teeth much like a dog uses its nose, looking to gather information about what comes across their path. Defensive reaction. It may seem counterintuitive but, while sharks often evoke a sense of fear in people, they are capable of being afraid, especially if they are startled by a person. Are shark attacks on people common? + No. People being attacked by sharks is rare. Before the fatal encounter between a white shark and a surfer in Wellfleet in the fall of 2018, the last person fatally attacked by a shark in Massachusetts was recorded in 1936. Drowning is a far more dangerous threat to public safety than a shark attack. However, while the relative risk of a shark attack posed to people is low, the potential for interactions between white sharks and people is elevated in areas where sharks gather to feed on seals, particularly in regions with high numbers of recreational water users (swimmers, surfers, body boarders, stand-up paddle-boarders, scuba divers, and kayakers). Are there times of the year that are particularly risky for shark encounters? + Based on the tagging data collected to date, we know that peak white shark activity along the coast of Cape Cod occurs from the summer through the fall. In this region, white sharks hunt for seals in nearshore waters, which is why we advise recreational water users to avoid areas where seals are present. The Massachusetts Division of Marine Fisheries has been tagging white sharks off the coast of Cape Cod, in collaboration with AWSC, for over a decade now to collect data and identify trends as it relates to how, or if, times of day, tidal conditions, and local topography affect shark behavior. Are the sharks mostly congregating along the outer Cape? + Certainly, the outer Cape is where we’ve had the most sightings. However, that’s also where researchers have concentrated their field studies. Other parts of the Cape still need to be surveyed to get a better idea of the presence of sharks in those areas. We do know that white sharks are large, mobile animals that are not naturally confined to one area. Based on tagging data that’s been collected we also know that sharks move frequently between the outer Cape and other regions (Cape Cod Bay, Gulf of Maine, Canada, New York Bight). Are there any areas where there are no sharks? + The waters surrounding Cape Cod are part of a wild ocean environment with a diversity of marine life, which includes many species of sharks – from sand tigers and threshers to basking and white sharks. Sharks are mobile animals that are not confined to any one area. Fresh water ponds or pools are the only place where you can swim on Cape Cod where you won’t find sharks of any kind. White Shark Public Safety Where is it safe to swim? + The ocean is a dynamic environment and beachgoers always need to be cautious when entering the water. The Atlantic White Shark Conservancy is committed to sharing information about white shark movements and behaviors with the public so that people decide for themselves how and where they use the water recreationally. What is being done to enhance public safety? + Various towns on the outer Cape and the Cape Cod National Seashore are leading the effort to better protect residents and tourists who visit our beaches. Approaches include new signage, better communication equipment, extending the lifeguard season, and deploying more ATV’s and shark bite first aid equipment. However, it’s important to note that, as is the case in other parts of the world where there are shark-human encounters, there is no single-source solution that ensures 100% guaranteed safety. In the event someone is bitten by a shark, first response will be critical. To assist in those efforts, the Atlantic White Shark Conservancy has partnered with local first-responders to offer “Stop The Bleed” training. To learn more about that initiative click here https://www.bleedingcontrol.org/ What technologies and/or deterrence techniques are being explored? + The Towns of Chatham, Orleans, Eastham, Wellfeet, Truro, and Provincetown, along with the Cape Cod National Seashore and the Atlantic White Shark Conservancy, hired independent researchers, The Woods Hole Group , to analyze a broad range of mitigation strategies that have been proposed by the local community, such as the use of drones, shark detection buoys, netting and barriers. It is important to understand which technologies/techniques may or may not work, as marine environments are complex and vary in multiple ways depending on the geographic location. What may be effective in South Africa or Australia may or may not be effective along the coast of Cape Cod. To view the Woods Hole Group Shark Mitigation Alternatives Analysis, visit: https://parkplanning.nps.gov/projectHome.cfm?projectId=91210 About the Atlantic White Shark Conservancy (AWSC) What is the best way to see white sharks? + White sharks are an amazing species! We offer safe and exciting expeditions to witness these fascinating apex predators in their natural habitat. To learn more about these opportunities or to book a reservation, please visist https://www.atlanticwhiteshark.org/white-shark-expeditions What is the AWSC Shark Center? + The AWSC Shark Center is our home in Chatham, MA, where visitors can get an in-depth look at one of the ocean's most magnificent and misunderstood species: the Great White Shark. At our Shark Center, which is open to the public seasonally, we have interactive exhibits, videos, displays, virtual reality experiences, and many other ways to learn about our one of Cape Cod's most captivating summer residents. For more information about the Shark Center, hours of operation, or directions please visit our Shark Center page at https://www.atlanticwhiteshark.org/shark-center-chatham Are there volunteer opportunities with the Atlantic White Shark Conservancy? + Yes! As a non-profit organization, we rely heavily on volunteers. Please visit our volunteer page to learn how you can join our team at https://www.atlanticwhiteshark.org/volunteer Do you have an internship program? + For college students and recent college graduates, we offer internships for various positions based on project needs for the season. To learn more about our internship program and how to apply please visit https://www.atlanticwhiteshark.org/internships Are you hiring? + If you are interested in employment with us, please check our employment page regularly for current job opportunities at https://www.atlanticwhiteshark.org/employment Do you accept donations? + As a non-profit, donations are the lifeblood of the Atlantic White Shark Conservancy. Donations directly fund our white shark research, public safety programs, outreach and education initiatives, as well as program expenses such as our outreach efforts, our research spotter pilot, underwater footage and our Gills Club initiative. Among the more popular ways to donate is through our buoy, name-a-tagged-shark, or Sharktivity App sponsorships. To learn more about our sponsorship opportunities, visit https://www.atlanticwhiteshark.org/sponsor or donate directly through our donor portal at http://www.atlanticwhiteshark.org/donate How do I book an Atlantic White Shark Conservancy representative for a lecture? + Our staff frequently speaks at forums and lectures at events. If you would like one of our representatives to speak at your event, please contact info@atlanticwhiteshark.org . We will travel just about anywhere in the New England area. Do you have youth programs? + To encourage more young girls to consider science, technology, engineering and math (STEM) careers -- we also have the Gills Club. The Gills Club is for girls 13 and younger. To get your child involved in the Gills Club please, click here to register http://www.gillsclub.org/events . We are always looking for female scientists to help with the Gills Club. If you are a female scientist and would like to get involved please contact us at gillsclub@atlanticwhiteshark.org Do you share your research on sharks? + Our primary mission is white shark research and education – all of which we share. To learn more about past and ongoing research, please visit https://www.atlanticwhiteshark.org/white-shark-research If you are an educator looking for a data set to be used for as part of your curriculum, please visit the education resources page for mock data, lesson plans, and other resources at https://www.atlanticwhiteshark.org/education-resources How do I get a white shark license plate? + Our white shark license plates are only available for vehicles registered in the state of Massachusetts. The special plate fee is $40 -- $28 of which tax deductible and donated to the Atlantic White Shark Conservancy. When you renew your plate after 2 years, the full $40 is donated. You can order your plate online through the Registry of Motor Vehicles at https://www.atlanticwhiteshark.org/white-shark-license-plates Do you sell merchandise? + We offer a variety of shark-themed merchandise at our Shark Center in Chatham and online. All proceeds from merchandise sales help fund our research and education initiatives. To place an online order, please visit https://atlantic-white-shark-conservancy.myshopify.com/ Media/Interview Requests + All press inquiries and/or interview requests can be submitted to awsc@denterlein.com Still need answers?  Search our site here No results found OTHERWISE, WE ARE ALWAYS HAPPY TO CONNECT WITH OUR COMMUNITY. PLEASE USE THE CONTACT FORM TO GET IN TOUCH.

title: The Return of the Seals | Woods Hole Oceanographic Institution
text: There was once a bounty on gray seals in New England; hunters in Massachusetts and Maine got $5 if they turned in a nose or skin. From the 1890s until the 1960s, an estimated 135,000 seals were killed, and seals disappeared from Cape Cod. Then the federal Marine Mammal Protection Act of 1972 outlawed seal killing. Gradually the seal population recovered and is now thriving. A 1994 survey spotted 2,035 seals in Cape Cod waters; by 2011, the National Marine Fisheries Service counted more than 15,700, with hundreds regularly seen congregating on beaches, or “hauling out,” on the Cape shoreline. The population of humans has also flourished. Never in their lifetimes had they encountered seals restored to pre-hunting levels. Perhaps inevitably, conflicts have ensued. In recent years, people have complained that the growing seal herds are attracting great white sharks to Cape Cod waters, eating fish that fishermen hoped to catch, and polluting beaches with seal feces. In 2011, five seals on Cape Cod were found shot in the head. To help address these concerns, a group of scientists, fishers, and resource managers created the Northwest Atlantic Seal Consortium in 2012. Its goal is to get and share knowledge on the ecological role of seals in the northeastern United States: how they live, where they go, what they eat, their health and illnesses, and their interactions with the world—including humans—around them. In an initial effort, Woods Hole Oceanographic Institution biologist Rebecca Gast investigated the claim that seal poop may be contaminating water off Cape Cod beaches. “As far as I know, no one had looked at the data to ask these questions before,” Gast said. She and colleagues examined water quality data routinely collected by the Massachusetts Department of Public Health from 89 public beaches between 2003 and 2012. The sites included beaches in six towns near where seals haul out: Provincetown, Truro, Wellfleet, Eastham, Orleans, and Chatham. In particular, she examined how many times levels of bacteria associated with fecal contamination exceeded limits for public health and triggered beach closures. “Our analysis of 10 years of data shows there was no change in the trend of water quality exceedances for the region,” Gast said. Looking more closely at the beaches closest to large seal haul-outs, the researchers found that beaches within five miles of the haul-outs actually showed a slight decreasing trend in contamination incidences and beach closures over the past decade, while the beaches more than five miles away from seal haul-outs showed a slight increasing trend in beach closures. “The evidence indicates that at this time, the water quality at beaches near large seal haul-outs is not worse than at beaches without large numbers of seals nearby,” Gast concluded. “In fact, four of the five beaches in Chatham Harbor that are close to the seal haul-outs have never had an exceedance event.”

title: Training induces changes in white-matter architecture | Nature Neuroscience
text: Abstract Although experience-dependent structural changes have been found in adult gray matter, there is little evidence for such changes in white matter. Using diffusion imaging, we detected a localized increase in fractional anisotropy, a measure of microstructure, in white matter underlying the intraparietal sulcus following training of a complex visuo-motor skill. This provides, to the best of our knowledge, the first evidence for training-related changes in white-matter structure in the healthy human adult brain. title: Training-induced brain structure changes in the elderly - PubMed
text:
Full text links Cite Display options Display options Format Abstract PubMed PMID Linked Discoveries Abstract It has been suggested that learning is associated with a transient and highly selective increase in brain gray matter in healthy young volunteers. It is not clear whether and to what extent the aging brain is still able to exhibit such structural plasticity. We built on our original study, now focusing on healthy senior citizens. We observed that elderly persons were able to learn three-ball cascade juggling, but with less proficiency compared with 20-year-old adolescents. Similar to the young group, gray-matter changes in the older brain related to skill acquisition were observed in area hMT/V5 (middle temporal area of the visual cortex). In addition, elderly volunteers who learned to juggle showed transient increases in gray matter in the hippocampus on the left side and in the nucleus accumbens bilaterally. Flow chart of volunteer recruitment. Only 10 of 44 individuals were able to juggle 60 s at time point 2. Fifteen volunteers were fluent jugglers and accomplished between 40 and 60 s. We therefore compared the data of 25 individuals of the jugglers group who had the best results in endurance juggling (mean time, 56.7 s) with the data sets of the 25 controls. Figure 2. Time point (before intervention, after… Figure 2. Time point (before intervention, after intervention) by group (jugglers, controls) interaction analysis, testing… Figure 2. Time point (before intervention, after intervention) by group (jugglers, controls) interaction analysis, testing for greater changes in the jugglers group. Gray-matter increase is shown superimposed on a normalized T1 image. The left side of the picture is the left side of the brain. A , A significant gray-matter expansion was found in hMT/V5 on the right side. This area is virtually the same area as demonstrated previously (Draganski et al., 2004). The box plot shows relative gray-matter change in the peak voxel in the right hMT for all jugglers over the three time points (error bars indicate the SD, range, and the mean for each time point). B , C , Only the jugglers group, but not the controls, showed a significant gray-matter increase in the hippocampus on the left side ( B ) and the nucleus accumbens bilaterally ( C ). This increase of gray matter reversed when study participants were examined at time point 3 (after the weeks without practicing). title: Apple introduces the new 14-inch MacBook Pro with M6 - Apple
text: PRESS RELEASE October 27, 2026 Apple introduces the new 14‑inch MacBook Pro with M6 Supercharged by M6, the 14-inch MacBook Pro features incredible performance and next-level AI capabilities, enhanced connectivity, and up to 24 hours of battery life, delivering even more value Supercharged by the all-new M6 chip, the 14-inch MacBook Pro brings extraordinary performance, AI capabilities, and up to 24 hours of battery life — making it an even more compelling value. CUPERTINO, CALIFORNIA Apple today announced the new 14-inch MacBook Pro with M6 , delivering even more performance, powerful on-device AI capabilities, and faster connectivity for college students, business users, creators, and more. M6 features an advanced 12-core CPU with the world’s fastest CPU core, so everything from productivity tasks to more demanding pro workflows feels incredibly fast and responsive. 1 The 12-core GPU delivers up to 30 percent faster graphics and up to 25 percent faster AI workloads when compared to M5, making the 14-inch MacBook Pro with M6 a compelling value for users who need serious power. 2 For those upgrading from M1, the performance gains are even more significant, with up to 11x faster graphics and up to 13x faster AI performance. 3 With additional Neural Accelerators in the GPU and a Dual 16-core Neural Engine, M6 turns MacBook Pro into an even more powerful platform for AI — from taking advantage of Siri AI and Apple Intelligence features across apps and macOS to running LLMs locally, all while preserving user privacy. 4 In addition, the 14-inch MacBook Pro features Wi-Fi 7 and Bluetooth 6, while superfast storage makes working with large files, exporting projects, and running demanding AI workflows fly. And with phenomenal battery life of up to 24 hours, it delivers the same remarkable performance whether plugged in or on battery, so users can work, create, and pursue their passions from anywhere. 3 It also offers the advanced features users love, including the stunning Liquid Retina XDR display with a nano-texture option, a 12MP Center Stage camera, an immersive six-speaker sound system, and a wide array of ports. Together with macOS 27, the new 14-inch MacBook Pro with M6 is a major upgrade for existing Mac users and those coming to Mac for the first time. Available in space black and silver, it can be pre-ordered beginning tomorrow, October 28, with availability starting Friday, November 6. The new 14-inch MacBook Pro with M6 combines next-generation performance and powerful on-device AI in a portable design, empowering students, creatives, developers, and business professionals to take their workflows anywhere. “The 14-inch MacBook Pro is the pro laptop of choice for a wide range of users — from college students, to business professionals across every industry, to multidisciplinary creators doing it all on one device,” said Shelly Goldberg, Apple’s vice president of Hardware Engineering. “With the powerful M6 chip, we’re taking performance to the next level, with a boost in CPU speed and graphics and even more powerful capabilities for on-device AI. With its amazing battery life, remarkable Liquid Retina XDR display, and even faster connectivity, the new 14-inch MacBook Pro with M6 delivers a fantastic combination of performance, capability, and value.” M6 makes the 14-inch MacBook Pro faster than ever, thanks to a powerful 12-core CPU, advanced 12-core GPU, and Dual 16-core Neural Engine. M6: Blazing-Fast Performance and On-Device AI Capabilities M6 brings even more performance and next-level AI capabilities to the 14-inch MacBook Pro. Featuring a powerful 12-core CPU, a 12-core GPU with Neural Accelerators in each core, Dual 16-core Neural Engine, and faster unified memory, MacBook Pro with M6 is faster and more responsive. The 12-core CPU, with two more cores than before, brings blazing-fast single- and multithreaded performance, so users can fly through everything from multitasking across apps to compiling code to handling complex creative workflows. The 12-core GPU, also with two additional cores, delivers up to 30 percent faster graphics performance when compared to M5. 2 Everything from 3D modeling to photo editing and gaming feels incredibly fast, enhanced by a third-generation ray-tracing engine and Dynamic Caching to optimize on-chip memory. It also brings up to 25 percent faster performance for on-device AI workloads, like LLM prompt processing, compared to M5. 3 The Dual 16-core Neural Engine delivers up to 1.9x faster performance than M5 and works with the advanced GPU to dramatically accelerate AI workloads like image generation, Super Resolution, and AI upscaling. 2 The Neural Engine also powers Apple Intelligence, enabling advanced and energy-efficient on-device AI processing. The 14-inch MacBook Pro with M6 does all this with industry-leading performance per watt and up to 24 hours of battery life, the longest ever in a Mac. With 16GB of unified memory standard, configurable up to 32GB, and higher memory bandwidth up to 170GB/s, MacBook Pro makes multitasking and working with demanding apps and large projects even faster. The 14-inch MacBook Pro with M6 helps motion designers model 3D objects, design product visualizations, and render animations with ease. The 14-inch MacBook Pro with M6 enables : 3 Up to 13x faster time to first token performance for LLM prompt processing compared to the 13-inch MacBook Pro with M1, and up to 1.3x faster than the 14-inch MacBook Pro with M5. Up to 11.7x faster render performance with ray tracing in Blender compared to the 13-inch MacBook Pro with M1, and up to 1.3x faster than the 14-inch MacBook Pro with M5. Up to 3.3x faster image-processing performance in Affinity compared to the 13-inch MacBook Pro with M1, and up to 1.2x faster than the 14-inch MacBook Pro with M5. Up to 2.5x faster project build performance when compiling code in Xcode compared to the 13-inch MacBook Pro with M1, and up to 1.3x faster than the 14-inch MacBook Pro with M5. Film editors and content creators can quickly and efficiently composite visual effects and add cinematic motion graphics in popular video editing tools on the 14-inch MacBook Pro with M6. Photographers and designers can make complex AI-powered image adjustments in real time using apps like Pixelmator Pro on the 14-inch MacBook Pro with M6. Developers can build and test their apps with blazing-fast compile times in Xcode on the 14-inch MacBook Pro with M6. A Huge Upgrade with Even More Value There’s never been a better time for customers to upgrade from a previous-generation MacBook Pro with Apple silicon or an Intel-based Mac. The 14-inch MacBook Pro with M6 delivers remarkable value thanks to major performance improvements and powerful AI capabilities. The new 14-inch MacBook Pro also features all of the compelling capabilities that have made it so popular, including: Phenomenal battery life : In addition to the huge leap in performance, battery life gets up to 14 additional hours for Intel-based upgraders and up to four more hours for users coming from M1, delivering up to 24 hours overall, so users can get more done on a single charge. Users coming from Intel-based and M1 systems will also get 16GB of starting unified memory, an additional Thunderbolt port, and the space black finish with an anodization seal for fewer fingerprints. A brilliant pro display : The stunning Liquid Retina XDR display delivers up to 1600 nits of peak HDR brightness and a 1,000,000:1 contrast ratio, bringing HDR photos and videos to life with deep blacks, brilliant highlights, and vibrant colors. And for users working in bright or challenging lighting conditions, a nano-texture display option dramatically reduces reflections and glare. Powerful connectivity : Now with Wi-Fi 7 and Bluetooth 6, the 14-inch MacBook Pro delivers fast wireless performance and low latency, along with support for up to two external displays. Its versatile array of ports — including the HDMI, MagSafe 3, and three Thunderbolt 4 ports; an SDXC card slot; and a headphone jack — makes it easy to connect high-speed peripherals, transfer photos, or expand a workspace. Advanced camera, mics, and speakers : A 12MP Center Stage camera with Desk View helps keep users perfectly framed on video calls, while a studio-quality three-mic array and amazing six-speaker sound system with Spatial Audio deliver an immersive audio experience. Fast charging : MacBook Pro with M6 supports fast charging, reaching up to 50 percent charge in just 30 minutes when paired with a compatible higher-wattage USB-C power adapter, such as the 96W Power Adapter. 3 A laptop that’s built to last : With an enclosure made from 100 percent recycled aluminum, MacBook Pro is exceptionally durable and can stand up to everyday use for years to come. Better together with iPhone : When used together with Continuity, iPhone and Mac are even more powerful — letting users move seamlessly across devices to share files and photos, hand off tasks, and even control their iPhone from their 14-inch MacBook Pro. 5 Users switching to Mac for the first time can use iPhone to conveniently and securely transfer settings, files, photos, passwords, and more. The brilliant Liquid Retina XDR display delivers up to 1600 nits of peak HDR brightness and a 1,000,000:1 contrast ratio. HDR photos and videos look more true to life with deep blacks, brilliant highlights, and vibrant colors. With the new 14-inch MacBook Pro, users can connect high-speed peripherals, transfer photos, work with multiple external displays, and more with its wide array of ports. macOS 27 Golden Gate The new 14-inch MacBook Pro with M6 comes to life with macOS 27, which includes Siri AI, a profoundly more capable, conversational, and personal assistant; helpful Apple Intelligence features across everyday apps; and improvements that make the Mac even more responsive and reliable. Siri AI can draw on personal context to help users find what they need in the moment across messages, emails, photos, and more; answer questions about virtually any topic; and get things done across apps — all with groundbreaking privacy protections. Siri AI is integrated into Spotlight and systemwide context menus, and users can ask Siri about what’s on their display with Visual Intelligence using a dedicated keyboard shortcut. Users can also write and edit with Siri almost anywhere they type. Additionally, Apple Intelligence makes apps smarter and more useful. In Safari, it powers new tools that automatically organize a user’s tabs into topics; notify them of website changes, like product restocks or price drops; and enable the creation of custom extensions based on a description. Users can also easily create an automation in Shortcuts by simply describing it, or tap into intelligent photo editing tools in the Photos app. The new 14-inch MacBook Pro gets even more responsive, reliable, and delightful with refinements to design, performance, search, and more. Updates to Liquid Glass deliver an even more focused and approachable experience. A new slider in Settings gives users the option to personalize Liquid Glass, adjusting it anywhere from ultraclear to fully tinted to match their preference, and app icons are sharper and more defined. 14-inch MacBook Pro with M6 and the Environment The new 14-inch MacBook Pro with M6 was built with the environment in mind and drives progress toward Apple’s ambitious plan to be carbon neutral across its entire footprint by 2030. It is made with 45 percent recycled content overall, 6 including 100 percent recycled aluminum in the enclosure, 100 percent recycled cobalt in the battery, and, in a first for Apple, 100 percent recycled tantalum in multiple capacitors. It is manufactured with 60 percent renewable electricity, such as wind and solar, across the supply chain. The 14-inch MacBook Pro with M6 is designed to be durable and repairable, and meets Apple’s high standards for energy efficiency and safe chemistry. As with all Apple products, its paper packaging is 100 percent fiber-based 7 and designed to be recycled. Pricing and Availability Customers can pre-order the new 14-inch MacBook Pro with M6 starting tomorrow, October 28, on apple.com/store and in the Apple Store app in 35 countries and regions, including the U.S. It will begin arriving to customers, and in Apple Store locations and Apple Authorized Resellers, starting Friday, November 6. The 14-inch MacBook Pro with M6 starts at $1,999 (U.S.) and $1,899 (U.S.) with education savings . Additional technical specifications and configure-to-order options are available at apple.com/macbook-pro . With Apple Upgrade , eligible customers in the U.S. can lease a new Mac with low monthly payments and easily upgrade at the end of their lease. 8 Lease the 14-inch MacBook Pro with M6 with Apple Upgrade from $38.99 (U.S.) per month, excluding taxes and any trade-in credit, for 36 months.^ With Apple Trade In, customers can trade in their current computer and get credit toward a new Mac. Customers can visit apple.com/shop/trade-in to see what their device is worth. With year-round education pricing — available to current and newly accepted college students and educators — customers can save on MacBook Pro, along with a wide range of products and services through the Apple Store online and in stores. Visit the Apple Education Store for details. Customers in the U.S. who shop at Apple using Apple Card 9 can pay monthly at 0 percent APR when they choose to check out with Apple Card Monthly Installments, 10 and they’ll get 3 percent Daily Cash back — all up front. More information — including details on eligibility, exclusions, and Apple Card terms — is available at apple.com/apple-card/monthly-installments . AppleCare delivers exceptional service and support, with flexible options for Apple users. Customers can choose AppleCare+ to cover their new Mac or, in available markets, AppleCare One to protect multiple products in one simple plan. Both plans include coverage for accidents like drops and spills, theft and loss protection on eligible products, battery replacement service, and priority support from Apple Experts. In the U.S., customers can also choose AppleCare One Family, which extends that same coverage to every eligible device across an Apple Family Sharing group for one fixed monthly price. For more information, visit apple.com/applecare . Every customer who buys directly from Apple gets access to Personal Setup. In these guided one-on-one online sessions, a Specialist can walk them through setup or focus on features that will help them make the most of their new device. Customers can also learn more about getting started and going further with their new device with a Today at Apple session at their nearest Apple Store. Better together with iPhone : When used together with Continuity, iPhone and Mac are even more powerful — letting users move seamlessly across devices to share files and photos, hand off tasks, and even control their iPhone from their 14-inch MacBook Pro. 5 Users switching to Mac for the first time can use iPhone to conveniently and securely transfer settings, files, photos, passwords, and more. macOS 27 Golden Gate The new 14-inch MacBook Pro with M6 comes to life with macOS 27, which includes Siri AI, a profoundly more capable, conversational, and personal assistant; helpful Apple Intelligence features across everyday apps; and improvements that make the Mac even more responsive and reliable. Siri AI can draw on personal context to help users find what they need in the moment across messages, emails, photos, and more; answer questions about virtually any topic; and get things done across apps — all with groundbreaking privacy protections. Siri AI is integrated into Spotlight and systemwide context menus, and users can ask Siri about what’s on their display with Visual Intelligence using a dedicated keyboard shortcut. Users can also write and edit with Siri almost anywhere they type. Additionally, Apple Intelligence makes apps smarter and more useful. In Safari, it powers new tools that automatically organize a user’s tabs into topics; notify them of website changes, like product restocks or price drops; and enable the creation of custom extensions based on a description. Users can also easily create an automation in Shortcuts by simply describing it, or tap into intelligent photo editing tools in the Photos app. The new 14-inch MacBook Pro gets even more responsive, reliable, and delightful with refinements to design, performance, search, and more. Updates to Liquid Glass deliver an even more focused and approachable experience. A new slider in Settings gives users the option to personalize Liquid Glass, adjusting it anywhere from ultraclear to fully tinted to match their preference, and app icons are sharper and more defined. 14-inch MacBook Pro with M6 and the Environment The new 14-inch MacBook Pro with M6 was built with the environment in mind and drives progress toward Apple’s ambitious plan to be carbon neutral across its entire footprint by 2030. It is made with 45 percent recycled content overall, 6 including 100 percent recycled aluminum in the enclosure, 100 percent recycled cobalt in the battery, and, in a first for Apple, 100 percent recycled tantalum in multiple capacitors. It is manufactured with 60 percent renewable electricity, such as wind and solar, across the supply chain. The 14-inch MacBook Pro with M6 is designed to be durable and repairable, and meets Apple’s high standards for energy efficiency and safe chemistry. As with all Apple products, its paper packaging is 100 percent fiber-based 7 and designed to be recycled. The 14-inch MacBook Pro with M6 starts at $1,999 (U.S.) and $1,899 (U.S.) with education savings . Additional technical specifications and configure-to-order options are available at apple.com/macbook-pro . With Apple Upgrade , eligible customers in the U.S. can lease a new Mac with low monthly payments and easily upgrade at the end of their lease. 8 Lease the 14-inch MacBook Pro with M6 with Apple Upgrade from $38.99 (U.S.) per month, excluding taxes and any trade-in credit, for 36 months.^ With Apple Trade In, customers can trade in their current computer and get credit toward a new Mac. Customers can visit apple.com/shop/trade-in to see what their device is worth. With year-round education pricing — available to current and newly accepted college students and educators — customers can save on MacBook Pro, along with a wide range of products and services through the Apple Store online and in stores. Visit the Apple Education Store for details. Customers in the U.S. who shop at Apple using Apple Card 9 can pay monthly at 0 percent APR when they choose to check out with Apple Card Monthly Installments, 10 and they’ll get 3 percent Daily Cash back — all up front. More information — including details on eligibility, exclusions, and Apple Card terms — is available at apple.com/apple-card/monthly-installments . Customers can choose AppleCare+ to cover their new Mac or, in available markets, AppleCare One to protect multiple products in one simple plan. Both plans include coverage for accidents like drops and spills, theft and loss protection on eligible products, battery replacement service, and priority support from Apple Experts. For more information, visit apple.com/applecare . Every customer who buys directly from Apple gets access to Personal Setup. In these guided one-on-one online sessions, a Specialist can walk them through setup or focus on features that will help them make the most of their new device. title: Russia suffers record troop losses in October, its worst month since full-scale invasion, Ukraine says
text: War Russia suffers record troop losses in October, its worst month since full-scale invasion, Ukraine says November 1, 2026 11:30 am • 3 min read Prefer on Google by Chris Powers Photo for illustrative purposes: A fallen Russian soldier's belongings in Donetsk Oblast, Ukraine on Feb. 24, 2024.(Jose Colon/Anadolu via Getty Images) Russia's combat losses were greater in October 2026 than in any other month since Moscow launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022, the General Staff of Ukraine's Armed Forces reported. According to the data from the General Staff, Russia's estimated losses reached 54,400 soldiers in October. That's 8,170 more than in the previous month. The figure includes those killed, wounded, and missing in action. "This is a record for any month of the full-scale war," said President Volodymyr Zelensky on social media. Zelensky also mentioned that in October, Ukraine liberated more territory than it lost, 96.2 square kilometers (37.1 square miles) vs 85.8 square kilometers (33.1 square miles) occupied by Russia. In October, our Ukrainian Defence Forces inflicted record losses on the enemy and recaptured more territory than the Russian occupiers were able to seize. "We thank all our defenders, all our soldiers, every brigade and every unit for this result, which is so important for our country. Russia is losing," Zelensky said. The General Staff said the high rate matters because it "exceeds the enemy's ability to replenish its units. Every month of the war is costing the Russian army more and more." The National Guard's 1st Azov Corps said a significant share of Moscow's losses stemmed from Russia's offensive in the direction of the city of Dobropillia , in Donetsk Oblast. A Month of Record Losses for Russian Occupiers In October, Russian forces suffered their highest personnel losses since 2022. A significant portion of these losses occurred within the area of responsibility of the 1st Corps of the National Guard of Ukraine “Azov”, one of the key… pic.twitter.com/6bvn4NqUEU — First Corps Azov of the National Guard of Ukraine (@azov_media) October 31, 2026 The Corps estimates it has killed, wounded, and captured over 6,800 Russian troops in "one of the key axes of the Russian offensive." October was also a record month for Ukraine's Unmanned Systems Forces, its commander Robert "Magyar" Brovdi wrote on social media. Brovdi said that his forces hit a Russian soldier every 159 seconds in October, averaging 542 casualties daily. The more Russia racks up combat losses, the greater the need for Moscow to increase its own mobilization efforts. President Volodymyr Zelensky warned in August that Russia plans to mobilize around 300,000 people after its September election is out of the way. So far, Moscow announced plans to conscript an additional 120,000 people on Oct. 2. "Ukrainian Defense Forces will continue to inflict losses on the occupiers until the complete cessation of Russia's armed aggression against Ukraine," said the General Staff. According to the General Staff, Russia has lost 1,590,270 troops in Ukraine since the beginning of its full-scale invasion of Ukraine. The General Staff has not revealed its own losses during the full-scale invasion, citing operational secrecy. Independent Western think-tank reports agree that the Russian casualties significantly surpass Ukraine's losses, with the Center for Strategic and International Studies (CSIS) estimating the ratio to be "roughly 2.5:1 or 2:1." A January 2026 CSIS report said Ukraine has likely suffered between 500,000 and 600,000 casualties from February 2022 to December 2025, of which between 100,000 and 140,000 are thought to have been killed in action. read also ‘I don’t know if negotiated peace is achievable,’ Rubio says as uncertainty hangs over Russia-Ukraine talks Russia Ukraine Ukrainian armed forces Azov Russian armed forces Russian losses

title: Бійці “АЗОВУ” за жовтень 2026 року вбили на Добропільському напрямку понад 5 тисяч росіян, ще майже 2 тисячі дістали поранень
text: Ми в соціальних мережах 31 Жов, 2026 - 16:34 Євген Вакуленко Читати російською Зробити резюме статті: (ChatGPT) Підтримайте Вільне Радіо Щомісячно Одноразово Протягом жовтня 2026 року українські захисники з 1-го корпусу НГУ “АЗОВ” знищили 5017 росіян, ще 1820 дістали поранень, а 6 взяли в полон. Розповідаємо, скільки техніки російської армії знищили за цей місяць на Добропільському напрямку. Про втрати росіян розповіли в пресслужбу першого корпусу національної гвардії України “АЗОВ”. Крім російських військових, українські захисники у жовтні атакували й техніку армії загарбників. За цей місяць вдалося знищити: 5 бойових броньованих машин; 47 артилерійських систем; 2 РСЗВ; 469 одиниць автомобільної техніки; 2967 ударних і 183 розвідувальних БПЛА літакового типу; 2109 ударних та 268 розвідувальних БПЛА коптерного типу; 558 інженерно-фортифікаційних споруд і командних пунктів. Зазначимо, комунікаційники не уточнили, про який напрямок фронту йдеться. Водночас у 2026 році представники “АЗОВУ” неодноразово повідомляли , що виконують бойові завдання на Покровському напрямку. Зокрема , в районі Добропілля та Дружківки. Нагадаємо, захоплення Добропілля залишається головною стратегічною метою російської армії на Покровському напрямку фронту . Загарбники намагаються досягти цієї мети, аби посилити свої удари по українській логістиці. Представники ЗСУ запевняють, що в адміністративних межах Добропілля немає сталих або замаскованих позицій росіян. title: Adventurer arrives home after 28-year walk from South America
text: Homepage World Adventurer arrives home after 28-year walk from South America 'This is absolute madness. After 28 years, you couldn’t ask for more than this.' Angela Bushby welcomes her son Karl as he arrives back home in Hull following his 28 year walk from Chile. Picture: Annabel Lee-Ellis/Press Association Mon, 02 Nov, 2026 - 16:24 Dave Higgens       Adventurer Karl Bushby has been mobbed by well-wishers as he arrived in his home town of Hull in England on the last day of his 28-year walk from South America. Mr Bushby, now 57, told crowds in the city centre: “There has never been a welcome home quite like this.” The former paratrooper set off from the southern end of Chile in 1998, when he was 28, vowing to walk all the way home without using any form of motorised transport. On Monday, he made the penultimate stop of his epic journey in the centre of Hull, where he was greeted by hundreds of well-wishers outside the City Hall. He was mobbed and cheered as he walked into Queen Victoria Square wheeling his cart, before telling the crowd: “There has never been a welcome home quite like this, I’m sure. “This is absolute madness. After 28 years, you couldn’t ask for more than this. This is the last, last few steps.” Read More Crew from NASA's simulated Mars mission emerge after 378 days in isolation Mr Bushby was greeted by the lord mayor and Hull East MP Karl Turner, who read out a message of congratulations from British prime minister Andy Burnham. He went inside for a civic reception before setting off for the final leg of his 31,000-mile (50,000km) journey — the three miles to his mother’s house, in the north of the city, which he last visited in 1998. More crowds greeted Mr Bushby when he arrived at his final destination and gave his mother Angela a hug outside her terraced house. Among the others waiting for him in the front garden was his son Adam, who is now 36 but was eight when his father embarked on the adventure. Mr Bushby’s father Keith and his granddaughter were also among those posing for the mass of photographers. Neighbours from the surrounding estate came out to cheer him back, many having decorated their homes with “Welcome Home Karl” banners and flags. Karl Bushby (centre left) at a civic welcome in Queen Victoria Square as he arrives back home in Hull following his 28 year walk from Chile. Photo: Annabel Lee-Ellis/Press Association Monday’s leg crowns years of dangerous escapades, including crossing the notorious Darien Gap in Central America and traversing the Bering Strait between Alaska and Russia on the frozen sea. Mr Bushby arrived back in England earlier this month, announcing that he had swum the Channel. He told the crowd in the city centre: “Twenty-eight years… I could not have imagined this. One last enormous thank you, guys. Just an enormous thank you. “I guess I’ll be seeing you around. I’ll be knocking about for a while, I guess.” Mr Bushby said: “I didn’t do this alone. It was a big team. The biggest team – Earth. That’s what it took to get me back.” Lord mayor of Hull Maria Coward told Mr Bushby: “For 28 years – 10,229 days – Hull has been waiting for your return. Hull is proud of you. I’m proud of you. Everyone’s proud of you.” Mr Turner read Mr Burnham’s message of congratulations on what he described as an “extraordinary journey”. It said: “To walk around the world from Chile and back again is an achievement of truly remarkable proportions. It speaks of courage, resilience, perseverance and unbreakable spirit.” Karl Bushby: 'I didn’t do this alone. It was a big team. The biggest team – Earth.' Photo: Annabel Lee-Ellis/Press Association The prime minister’s statement also thanked Mr Bushby for his service to the country as a soldier. He said: “Your journey has taken nearly three decades, crossed continents and tested you in ways that most of us can barely imagine. “But today, as you return to the city from which you left 28 years ago, you bring something far greater than any world record or remarkable personal achievement. “You bring a story of what can be accomplished through extraordinary determination and self-belief.” X Looking for a thoughtful gift?​ Irish Examiner Gift subscriptions are now available. title: Charles left without umbrella in rainstorm fit for a king – ThePrint – ReutersFeed
text: Support our Journalism Depth, context and analysis Subscribe Home World Charles left without umbrella in rainstorm fit for a king World Charles left without umbrella in rainstorm fit for a king Reuters 02 November, 2026 05:30 pm IST Facebook Twitter WhatsApp Linkedin (c) Copyright Thomson Reuters 2026 Follow Us : Text Size: A- A+ SAINT GEORGE, Antigua and Barbuda, Nov 2 (Reuters) – King Charles flung up his hands in despair as he was caught in a tropical rainstorm in Antigua, while his wife Queen Camilla strolled off with the only available umbrella. The couple’s Caribbean tour has been dominated by the debate over Britain’s role in the slave trade, but it was the sight of the soaked monarch which made headlines on Sunday. As the rain hammered down on Charles, 77, he was seen gesturing and turning round to try to attract the attention of someone who might help, while Camilla was shielded from the downpour. Show Full Article Locals taking part in the Antigua and Barbuda independence day parade did not flinch as they were lashed by the storm. Charles was eventually given an umbrella and was seen joking about his experience with Prime Minister Gaston Browne. “I think I’m about to grow watercress on my suit,” he said in a video posted on the royal family’s Instagram account. It is not the first time the frustration of the famously short-fused Charles has been captured in public. Not long after he became king in 2022 in an incident which went viral on social media, he reacted grumpily when a pen leaked ink onto his hand at an event in Northern Ireland. “Oh God, I hate this,” he cursed. “I can’t bear this bloody thing… every stinking time,” he continued. He has since made fun of himself, quipping at a subsequent event, “I’m hoping that my pen is going to work. It doesn’t usually.” He is due to make a speech to Commonwealth leaders on Tuesday. Since becoming king, he has expressed sorrow for the suffering caused by slavery without crossing a line that Britain has long resisted: an apology. title: The King and Queen will visit Antigua and Barbuda, and His Majesty will visit The Bahamas and Guyana | The Royal Family
text: The King and Queen will visit Antigua and Barbuda, and His Majesty will visit The Bahamas and Guyana Published 02/10/2026 Their Majesties The King and Queen will undertake an Autumn Tour from Tuesday 27th October to Wednesday 4th November 2026. This will include visits to The Bahamas, Guyana and Antigua and Barbuda, as well as attendance at the Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting (CHOGM) 2026. The programme will reflect themes that are central to The King and Queen's public work, including environmental sustainability, biodiversity, community resilience, youth engagement and the Commonwealth. Across all three countries, Their Majesties will meet community leaders, young people, volunteers and those working to strengthen local communities and protect the natural environment. The Bahamas His Majesty's visit to The Bahamas will begin in Nassau, where he will attend a Youth Rally celebrating the contribution of young people to national life. During the visit, The King will also spend time with members of the Royal Bahamas Defence Force at Coral Harbour Base and attend engagements highlighting environmental conservation and sustainability. The programme will also include a sports engagement and a visit to Parliament Square, where His Majesty will meet representatives from across Bahamian society. In addition, The King will hold audiences and attend a Garden Reception, bringing together community leaders and guests from across the country. Guyana In Guyana, His Majesty will visit Georgetown, where the programme will reflect both the country's rich natural heritage and its leadership on environmental issues. The King will visit the Commonwealth War Graves and learn about efforts to preserve and celebrate Guyana's history and legacy. His Majesty will also attend a garden visit and participate in engagements connected to biodiversity and conservation, including the Global Biodiversity Alliance Conference. The programme will provide opportunities to meet representatives from communities and organisations working to protect the natural environment and promote sustainable development. The King will additionally attend an engagement with the National Toshaos Council, recognising the important contribution of Indigenous communities, before joining a Business Reception celebrating innovation, enterprise and economic partnership. His Majesty will also visit Georgetown's Seawall, a significant landmark for residents and visitors alike. Antigua and Barbuda Their Majesties will visit Antigua and Barbuda ahead of CHOGM 2026, with engagements that celebrate the nation's culture, heritage and communities. The King and Queen will attend a Church Service and the country's Independence Day Parade at the Sir Vivian Richards Stadium, where they will join celebrations marking this important national occasion. Their Majesties will also visit Government House and take part in a garden visit, while The King's programme will include engagements focused on the natural environment, heritage and sustainable development. These will include a visit highlighting environmental conservation and a meeting with business leaders at the Sticky Wicket Business Forum. Her Majesty will undertake separate engagements reflecting her longstanding interests, including a visit to the American University and an engagement with a local school. CHOGM 2026 As Head of the Commonwealth, The King, accompanied by The Queen, will attend the Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting in Antigua and Barbuda. Their Majesties will participate in the CHOGM Opening Ceremony and attend the CHOGM Dinner alongside leaders from across the Commonwealth. His Majesty will also host a Reception for New Heads of Government and attend engagements connected to the wider CHOGM programme, while Their Majesties will undertake visits in Antigua and Barbuda that celebrate the country's role as host nation. The tour will conclude on Wednesday 4th November with Their Majesties' departure from Antigua and Barbuda. title: Limpet Mines Return as Iran Hits Tankers Near Hormuz
text: Nov 1, 2026 7 min read Limpet Mines Return to the Gulf as Iran Strikes Four Tankers Near the Strait of Hormuz What’s inside? At a Glance Since October 29, Iran has attacked at least four tankers in and around the Strait of Hormuz . One attack used explosive devices fixed to a tanker’s hull by a small boat, the first use of limpet mines in the Gulf region since at least 2019. Three of the four tankers had been operating dark, and at least two are assessed as part of the “STS shuttle” moving Gulf cargoes through the Strait. Iranian sources claimed four tankers hit mines in the Strait and caught fire, though it is unclear whether that refers to vessels beyond the four confirmed. Transits have not slowed, with about 24 AIS -visible transits between October 30 and the morning of November 1, compared with 18 in the same window two days earlier. Four Tankers Hit in Three Days Between October 29 and 30, Iran attacked at least four tankers across the Strait of Hormuz and the waters around it. The attacks ranged from projectiles to hull-mounted explosives, and they struck laden and empty vessels, Qatari- and UAE-owned tonnage, and tankers that had spent weeks operating dark. Iranian sources separately claimed that four tankers hit mines in the Strait and caught fire, but it is unclear whether they were referring to additional vessels beyond the four confirmed. Projectiles Strike a Laden LNG Carrier Inside the Gulf On October 30, AL MAYEDA (IMO 9397298) , a Marshall Islands-flagged, Qatari-owned LNG carrier, laden with an unknown quantity of LNG according to Vortexa , was struck by three projectiles around 18:00 UTC, approximately 40 nautical miles south of Lavan Island. Windward data show AL MAYEDA turning around at 18:33 UTC before going dark at 22:17 UTC. AL MAYEDA had previously been dark between September 27 and October 30, and crossed inbound through the Strait of Hormuz during that period. AL MAYEDA’s track south of Lavan Island on October 30, 2026, showing the turnaround at 18:33 UTC after it was struck, before the vessel went dark. Source: Windward Maritime AI™ Platform. Limpet Mines Return to the Gulf The same day, a small boat approached LOUISE 1 (IMO 9290323) , a Panama-flagged, Panama-owned crude oil tanker, approximately 25 nautical miles northeast of Khasab, Oman, and emplaced two explosive devices on its hull. The explosion caused a fire in the engine room and briefly disabled the vessel. LOUISE 1 was last reported laden with 1.02 million barrels of crude on September 28, according to Vortexa, at its last AIS-reported position 12 nautical miles east of Khor Fakkan. It has not reported a position since. Dark Shuttle Tankers Come Under Fire Two more tankers were hit while likely transiting the Strait dark . RITI (IMO 9249075) , a Panama-flagged, Marshall Islands-owned crude oil tanker in ballast, according to Vortexa, was attacked in the Strait on October 30, likely during a dark inbound transit, and caught fire. Oman evacuated 25 crew members from the vessel 1.6 nautical miles off the Musandam Peninsula. RITI’s last known AIS position was on October 29, approximately 36 nautical miles east of Khor Fakkan. NASA FIRMS imagery did not detect a thermal anomaly off Musandam during this period, likely indicating the fire was extinguished. On October 29, ARZANAH (IMO 9928023) , a Liberia-flagged, UAE-owned crude oil tanker, was targeted while transiting an undisclosed part of the Strait. Vortexa last reported it laden with 2.14 million barrels of crude on October 17, and it has been dark since that date. Why the Return of Limpet Mines Matters This latest round of attacks continues the trend established this month while expanding the methods Iran is using. Limpet mines are a cost-effective weapon against tankers. They were last successfully used in the region in 2019, when multiple tankers were targeted at anchorages in the Gulf of Oman. The shift matters because it widens the threat beyond projectiles. A small boat that can approach a tanker and place explosives on its hull turns any slow-moving or anchored vessel into a potential target, including the dark shuttle tankers that rely on staying off AIS to avoid detection. This threat is particularly acute inside the Strait, where the ability to maneuver is already limited and small boats are regularly moving inside the waterway. Transits Are Still Rising The attacks, along with ongoing rhetoric about a possible resumption of combat operations in the Middle East, have not reduced Strait of Hormuz transits. Between October 30 and the morning of November 1, there were approximately 24 AIS-visible transits, compared with 18 AIS-visible transits in the same window between October 28 and 30. Shipowners continue to show a willingness to transit the Strait despite almost daily attacks from Iran. This very likely reflects the attraction of high freight rates for operators willing to take on the risk, and the continued push by Gulf States to move oil through the STS shuttle. Outlook That willingness has a limit. Should combat operations resume at a level of intensity similar to the first week of March, transits, already modest, would be expected to fall to near zero within the first 72 hours of the conflict as shipowners reassess the risk of exposure in the Strait. title: IRGC Claims Third Tanker Exploded by Sea Mine in Strait of Hormuz
text: News IRGC Claims Third Tanker Exploded by Sea Mine in Strait of Hormuz October 30, 2026 IranWire 2 min read The Public Relations Office of the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) Navy claimed on Friday afternoon, October 30, 2026, that a supertanker carrying over two million barrels of crude oil struck a sea mine at the mouth of the Strait of Hormuz, causing an explosion and setting the vessel ablaze. This assertion coincides with statements from the Commander of U.S. Central Command (CENTCOM), who released video footage showing that an aerial patrol over the Strait of Hormuz revealed no trace of IRGC forces. According to the IRGC Navy’s Friday statement, the burning supertanker marks the third vessel to suffer explosions and fires on Friday after transiting what the Islamic Republic deems “unauthorized” maritime routes. The announcement further noted that the supertanker was abandoned following the mine impact at the mouth of the Strait. However, details regarding the ship’s name, flag state, cargo owner, and crew condition were omitted. Previously, on Thursday, October 29, the IRGC reported that three tankers struck sea mines and caught fire while navigating the southern routes of the Strait of Hormuz. In a report on Thursday’s events, Agence France-Presse (AFP) noted that while the Iranian Armed Forces put the number of damaged tankers at four, these claims could not be independently verified. Conversely, the United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO) reported several maritime security incidents off the coast of Oman. According to UKMTO, one incident involved a small boat attaching two explosive devices to the hull of a tanker, triggering an explosion and an engine room fire, which was subsequently contained, with all crew members safe. UKMTO also reported an unidentified projectile hitting another tanker. It remains unconfirmed whether the maritime security incidents logged by the British agency correspond to the specific vessels referenced in the IRGC announcements. The IRGC’s claims regarding mine strikes emerge despite CENTCOM’s prior declarations that primary commercial shipping lanes through the Strait of Hormuz have been cleared via minesweeping operations. Rejecting CENTCOM’s claims, the IRGC continues to warn of hazards associated with traveling outside designated Iranian transit zones. Simultaneously, CENTCOM Commander Admiral Brad Cooper stated that during a flight over the Strait of Hormuz earlier in the week, he observed dozens of commercial ships, including oil and liquefied natural gas (LNG) tankers, navigating the waterway without any sign of IRGC forces. Cooper reiterated on Friday afternoon, October 30, that minesweeping operations had rendered the primary transit routes clear. title: Fact Check: Video Does NOT Show Attack On Netanyahu In October 2026 -- Footage Of Unrelated Incident In Bulgaria | Lead Stories
text: No Reports Does a viral video show a life-threatening attack on Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu one day after the Oct. 27, 2026, election? No, that's not true: The low quality of the video obscured that it showed a different politician giving a speech in a different country in 2013. It was Ahmed Dogan attacked in Bulgaria. The claim appeared in a post (archived here ) by @AsifAli_Haider on Oct. 28, 2026. It opened: Breaking 🚨 A very dangerous attack on Netanyahu in Tel Aviv it appears he has sustained severe injuries, and an aircraft is being dispatched to transport him to the United States. This is clearly evident from the footage. Don't remove my video X Twitter This is what a screenshot of the video looked like on X at the time of writing: (Image source: post by @AsifAli_Haider on X.) The claim emerged on social media when Israel was still counting votes (archived here ) cast in its Oct. 27, 2026, election (archived here ). The blurry 18-second clip included a fairly clear thumbnail depicting Netanyahu speaking in front of the wall with a Hebrew inscription. The opening frame, however, showed an acronym written in a Cyrillic alphabet: (Image source: post by @AsifAli_Haider on X.) (Image source: post by @AsifAli_Haider on X.) A reverse image search found a Jan. 20, 2013, BBC report about the incident (archived here ). That article, which featured a better-quality version of the video, reported that the footage showed an attack on Bulgarian politician Ahmed Dogan. He escaped unharmed. At the time, Dogan was the leader of the Movement for Rights and Freedoms whose acronym -- MRF -- is written as ДПС in Bulgarian (archived here ), the party's website confirms. Screenshots of the video the BBC used in its report as well as those of other media outlets (archived here ) demonstrate that the person at the podium bore no resemblance to Netanyahu: (Image source: BBC.) A broad search across sites indexed by Google News (archived here ) showed no media reports confirming any reports of a similar attack on Netanyahu on Oct. 28, 2026.

title: Ahmed Dogan attacked by armed assailant in Bulgaria - BBC News
text: Figure caption, The gunman did not succeed in making a shot A man put a gas pistol to the head of the leader of Bulgaria's ethnic Turkish party during a televised conference. Ahmed Dogan, leader of the Movement for Rights and Freedoms (MRF) was unharmed and the unidentified man was wrestled to the ground by security guards. The incident happened on Saturday at a party congress in the capital Sofia. Interior Minister Tsvetan Tsvetanov said the attacker, himself an ethnic Turk, tried to fire two shots but "most likely the gun misfired". Early reports suggested the weapon was a gun, but it was later confirmed to be a gas pistol - a non-lethal weapon used largely for self-defence which does not fire bullets but which can cause serious injuries if fired from close range. Mr Tsetanov also said the assailant had a criminal record for drugs possession, robberies and hooliganism. Police arrested the attacker, a 25-year-old from the Black Sea town of Burgas, who was also carrying two knives. The liberal MRF party represents ethnic Turks and other Muslims, who make up about 12% of Bulgaria's population of about seven million. Mr Dogan, 58, has led the party for almost 25 years. He returned to the party conference a few hours after the attack and was given a standing ovation. President Rosen Plevneliev said in a statement: "Bulgarian society is traditionally known for its tolerance, mutual acceptance and respect between different ethnic groups and religions. "Such an act is unacceptable in a democratic state." Attacks on politicians are rare in Bulgaria, but in 1996, former Prime Minister Andrei Lukanov was found shot dead near his home in Sofia. title: Erin Patterson appeals - judgment | The Supreme Court of Victoria
text: Judgment in relation to the appeals was handed down on Friday 30 October at 10am. The two appeals were an appeal by Erin Patterson for the Court of Appeal to review and overturn the findings of guilt from the trial (an appeal against conviction), and an appeal by the DPP against the sentence imposed. The Court of Appeal livestreamed the appeal decisions. Following a jury trial which ran from April to July last year, Ms Patterson was found guilty of murdering her parents-in-law Don and Gail Patterson and her aunt-in-law Heather Wilkinson. She was also found guilty of the attempted murder of her uncle-in-law Ian Wilkinson. Justice Christopher Beale sentenced Erin Patterson on Monday 8 September to life imprisonment with a non-parole period of 33 years. The full Court of Appeal judgment is available online . title: Mushroom murderer Erin Patterson likely to die in jail after failed appeal - ABC News
text: Mushroom murderer Erin Patterson likely to die in jail after failed appeal By court reporter Kristian Silva and Tim Callanan Topic: Courts Posted Fri 30 Oct 2026 at 10:13am Fri 30 Oct 2026 at 10:13am Fri 30 Oct 2026 at 10:13am , updated Fri 30 Oct 2026 at 3:53pm Fri 30 Oct 2026 at 3:53pm Fri 30 Oct 2026 at 3:53pm Erin Patterson was resentenced to life in prison without parole. ( NewsWire: Jason Edwards ) In short: Victoria's highest court has removed the possibility of parole for jailed triple murderer Erin Patterson. The court also rejected Patterson's appeal against her convictions for killing her relatives with a beef Wellington meal laced with death cap mushrooms. What's next? It is unclear whether Patterson's legal team will mount a challenge in the High Court. abc.net.au/news/erin-patterson-loses-mushroom-murder-convictions-appeal/107326714 Link copied Share Share article Erin Patterson will die in prison, after Victoria's highest court stripped the mushroom killer of a chance of parole and labelled her crimes "extraordinarily cold and calculated". In its judgment, published in full this afternoon, Victoria's Court of Appeal increased Patterson's sentence for poisoning her relatives and dismissed all grounds of her appeal. Patterson was last year sentenced to life in prison with a non-parole period of 33 years for the murders of Don and Gail Patterson and Heather Wilkinson, along with the attempted murder of Heather's husband Ian. The group were poisoned with death cap mushrooms that Patterson had baked into beef Wellingtons, which she served at a lunch in 2023. Today, appeal judges Stephen McLeish, Lesley Taylor and Peter Kidd decided to remove the non-parole period altogether, meaning Patterson's sentence will expire upon death. Loading... “This offending was extraordinarily cold and calculated and stands to be denounced in the strongest terms," the judges wrote. " On any view, these were heinous crimes. " They described Patterson's crime as a case "of such shocking criminality that it is inappropriate to fix a non-parole period". Few killers in Australia are serving life sentences with no parole. Some include Martin Bryant, who carried out the Port Arthur massacre, Snowtown killers John Bunting and Robert Wagner, and serial murderer Peter Dupas. It is unclear whether Patterson's legal team will mount a challenge in the High Court. ( ABC News: Anita Lester ) Justice McLeish described Patterson's actions as "carefully planned and deliberate". "The applicant's intent to murder all four victims was sustained for nearly three weeks from when she invited them to lunch, through to preparing and serving the poisoned meal and then throughout the protracted suffering and ultimate deaths that resulted," he said. Patterson, who watched the proceedings on a video link, sat back in her seat and appeared to stare blankly when the decision was announced. She is being held in the maximum security wing of the Dame Phyllis Frost women's prison. Erin Patterson's appeal rejected : Look back on how today's hearing unfolded in our blog. Outside the court, prosecutors, police investigators and supporters of Patterson's ex-husband Simon Patterson grinned broadly. It is unclear whether her legal team will mount a challenge in the High Court of Australia. In August, the prosecution argued Patterson's offending was in the "worst category" of murders, and called for the non-parole period to be scrapped. They also submitted the sentencing judge Christopher Beale erred by finding Patterson was likely to be held in solitary confinement "for years to come" because of her notoriety. Patterson left with few legal avenues The three judges of the appeal court also dismissed the 52-year-old's appeal against her convictions. In Patterson's conviction appeal, her lawyers argued her trial last year was compromised by what they described as a "catastrophic" arrangement, where members of the jury were in the same hotel as police and prosecutors . The appeal judges said the jury setup "offered fertile grounds for speculation" but there was no reason to believe a miscarriage of justice occurred. Patterson's other six appeal grounds were also unsuccessful. More on Erin Patterson 'She's no dope': Who is the host of Australia's most infamous lunch? They also dismissed claims the trial judge incorrectly ruled that an old SD card with mushroom photos and videos was inadmissible during the prosecution case; and that critical Facebook messages Patterson had written about her extended family should have been excluded. The defence had accused senior prosecutor Nanette Rogers SC of conducting an "unfair and oppressive" cross-examination of Patterson in the witness box. The appeal judges said Dr Rogers was "ably and fairly discharging her obligations" under the legal rule of Browne v Dunn, which require allegations to be put directly to a person under cross-examination. While the court found Dr Rogers's closing address had "some blemishes", it was not unfair. Finally, the court rejected claims the prosecution changed its case by telling the jury there was no motive, but then implied one existed by the end of the trial. The decision to reject Patterson's appeal leaves her with few legal options , including appealing to the High Court. Loading... title: Serbia Election Marks the End of an Era | Council on Foreign Relations
text: Council on Foreign Relations Articles Share By experts and staff Published October 27, 2026  10:20 p.m. Charles A. Kupchan CFR Expert Senior Fellow Ivana Saric CFR Editor Share Former Serbian President Aleksandar Vucic conceded defeat to a student-led opposition movement in Serbia’s October 25 parliamentary elections, ending his party’s fourteen years in power. Vucic had called snap elections in a bid to regain his previous post as prime minister, but the list led by his populist Serbian Progressive Party (SNS) managed just under 40 percent of the vote compared with around 53 percent for the opposition Student List. Pollsters and the Republic Electoral Commission estimated turnout at nearly 70 percent, which Reuters noted was the highest turnout since the breakup of Yugoslavia. The vote came after nearly two years of student-led protests sparked by the deaths of sixteen people when a canopy collapsed at a renovated railway station in Novi Sad, a disaster that protesters blamed on corruption and cronyism . Some opposition parliamentary parties supported the student movement, which demanded early elections. It put forth a list of 250 candidates—including doctors, professors, farmers, and activists. Most opposition parties declined to field their own candidates and urged supporters to back the Student List. Several ran anyway, although no non-minority list outside the Student List and the SNS-led coalition crossed the 3 percent threshold. Charles Kupchan, a senior fellow at the Council on Foreign Relations (CFR) and author of the new book Bringing Order to Anarchy: Governing the World to Come , spoke with CFR about the election results—and what they might mean—following his recent trip to Belgrade. You just returned from Belgrade. What was the mood like on the ground? I arrived last Thursday evening. In the city center, where my hotel was located, a massive protest was taking place; the crowd was estimated at around 150,000 people. The atmosphere was electric. The crowd was singing and chanting as it coursed through the streets, excited by the prospect that the Vucic era was about to come to an end. There were police everywhere and lots of streets cordoned off, but I saw no confrontations or violence. In my conversations on Friday and Saturday—I was at the University of Belgrade—students and faculty expressed cautious optimism that the Student List would prevail. In the end, a very high turnout helped the opposition win. Based on your conversations there, what were the main drivers of dissatisfaction with Vucic’s party? The student movement reflected a spontaneous mobilization of civil society that spread broadly across the country. One of the main slogans of this movement was “Serbia or the mafia,” indicating exasperation with years of corruption and state capture. The student movement now has wind in its sails and lots of political momentum. It needs to focus on turning that momentum into good policies and good governance. What does Vucic’s defeat mean for Serbia and its relationships with the European Union (EU), Russia, and its Balkan neighbors? It is difficult to say, because the Student List opposition campaigned mainly on domestic issues. Once a new government forms, it is likely to focus on fighting corruption, purging Vucic loyalists from the ministries and public enterprises, opening up a media community that had been dominated by Vucic, implementing economic reforms, and reducing political patronage. Relations with the EU are likely to improve as democratic reforms move forward. Ties to Russia may well grow more distant. Although it is unclear if the new government will try to move forward on relations with Kosovo, the change of government opens up the possibility of rekindling the normalization dialogue between Belgrade and Pristina. What challenges are ahead for the movement as it shifts to the task of governing? There is no clear leader of the Student List, and, as you noted, many of the winning candidates have little or no political experience. So the key challenge will be moving from a grassroots movement that inspired many voters across Serbia to governing a country that has long been run by Vucic and his embedded network of supporters. The movement has its work cut out. This work represents the views solely of the author(s).
