title: Serbian president concedes defeat to student-led movement in election - ABC News
text: Serbian president concedes defeat to student-led movement in election Topic: Elections Posted Mon 26 Oct 2026 at 8:06am Mon 26 Oct 2026 at 8:06am Mon 26 Oct 2026 at 8:06am , updated Mon 26 Oct 2026 at 11:53am Mon 26 Oct 2026 at 11:53am Mon 26 Oct 2026 at 11:53am Loading... In short: President Aleksandar Vučić has conceded defeat to a student-led protest movement in Serbia's parliamentary elections. Mr Vučić called a snap election in September after almost two years of student-led protests. What's next? Polls showed the students' candidate list would have 138 deputies, while Mr Vučić's SNS party garnered 104 seats in the 250-seat parliament. abc.net.au/news/serbia-election-vucic-defeat-student-protest/107307808 Link copied Share Share article Serbian President Aleksandar Vučić has conceded defeat to the student-led protest movement in parliamentary elections. "We still do not have final results [but] on the basis of a sample … it is clear that we have lost these elections," Mr Vučić said on Sunday. "The Student List has won. They will have between 135 and 140 seats, and we will have 105. Aleksandar Vučić ruled Serbia for 14 years. ( Reuters: Zorana Jevtic ) "No-one else has entered parliament." Mr Vučić called the snap elections in September, after almost two years of student-led demonstrations against perceived corruption and creeping authoritarianism. The protests were initially triggered by a train station canopy collapse in the city of Novi Sad in 2024 that killed 16 people. The election results follow almost two years of student-led protests against the government. ( Reuters: Marko Djurica ) Belgrade's streets erupted in celebration after Mr Vučić's announcement, with cars honking and students shouting "victory" and "he's done". "Dear Serbia, tonight the voice of the people is being heard," Radomir Sajcic, a professor at Belgrade University, said, speaking on behalf of the students at their headquarters. " Tonight we celebrate victory. Tomorrow we build the future. " People took to the streets of Belgrade to celebrate. ( Reuters: Zorana Jevtic ) Mr Vučić, endorsed by Russian President Vladimir Putin and denouncing the student movement as a foreign-led attempt to unseat him, led the Balkan country for 14 years. Turnout was nearly 70 per cent, the highest since the break-up of Yugoslavia in 1992. Lines snaked from polling stations in cities and towns across Serbia on Sunday, signalling a widespread desire for change. A large percentage of Serbians turned up to vote in this election. ( Reuters: Marko Djurica ) "For decades the people have been waiting for this time, something to bring hope that we can live freely and by the rules of democracy," said actor Jelena Stupljanin, 48, at a Belgrade polling station. Uncertainty over students' candidates A representative sample by the CESID-IPSPS pollsters showed the student's candidate list would have 138 deputies, while Mr Vučić's SNS party garnered 104 seats in the 250-seat parliament. The remaining seats will be shared between ethnic national minority parties. Much remains unclear about how the student-backed candidates will fare. Their list of 250 largely unknown personalities includes university professors, actors and farmers, and is led by cardiologist Ilija Srdanovic, although it is still unclear who will be prime minister. People celebrate the student movement's electoral victory. ( Reuters: Marko Djurica ) The students' domestic agenda aims to root out graft and improve schooling. Political analysts predict some kind of purge of Vučić allies in the police, security services and ministries. The students have been quieter about their international ambitions, but they will have to balance relations with China, a major investor; Russia, Serbia's traditional ally and main supplier of natural gas; and the European Union, Serbia's largest trading partner. title: Fact Check: Video Does NOT Show Moments Before 2026 Train Crash In Urda, Spain -- Was Originally Posted In 2020 | Lead Stories
text: 2020 Footage Does a video of jostled passengers show the moments inside a high-speed train before a fatal crash in Urda, Spain, on Oct. 28, 2026? No, that's not true: The video was posted on Facebook on Feb. 2, 2020, more than six years before that crash. The passenger who posted the 2020 video said in the caption that the Alvia train from Huelva to Madrid swayed back and forth the whole trip, leaving the passenger feeling nauseous. The claim appeared in a post (archived here ) by the @macronews account on X on Oct. 28, 2026. Translated from Spanish by Grok, it read: 🚨 Unforgivable tragedy! The worst railway accident in Europe in the last 80 years in Spain (46 dead). Passengers captured the violent jolt before the crash. Experts had warned about it and the government did nothing. 🚆⚠️ #España #Accidente #Noticias This is what a screenshot of the video in the post looked like at the time of publication: (Image source: post by @macronews on X.) The Spanish text caption on the video, translated by Google in advanced mode (archived here ), reads: THE VIDEO THAT REVEALS EVERYTHING! PASSENGER RECORDS THE SECONDS LEADING UP TO A HIGH-SPEED DERAILMENT IN SPAIN There was a fatal train crash in Urda, Spain, on Oct. 28, 2026. Associated Press (AP) reported (archived here ) at least 68 people have died as of publication. A state-owned RENFE high-speed train hit the back of a train run by a private company, IRYO, that was stopped on the tracks. This fact check does not address the post's claims about the death toll, the accident's historical ranking, prior warnings or government inaction. The video posted by @macronews does not show the moments before the Oct. 28, 2026, crash. Lead Stories ran a reverse image search and found that the footage in the post has been online for more than six years. The video appeared in a post (archived here ) made on Feb. 2, 2020, in a Facebook group (pictured below). The about section for the Facebook group Asociación Plataforma para la llegada de la L.A.V. a Huelva (archived here ) says it is an advocacy group to bring high-speed rail to the municipality of Huelva, Spain, and its province. The post included two videos showing the rocking action inside the train car. One video is 20 seconds long; the other is 12 seconds. The post was captioned in Spanish, translated by Google (archived here ): On the Alvia train from Huelva to Madrid, I spent the entire journey swaying back and forth--tossed from side to side the whole way, feeling completely nauseous. As always, Alvia just laughs in our faces. P.S. And the ticket cost €73--more expensive than an AVE ticket! (Image source: post by @moises.perezjimenez.96 on Facebook.)

title: Trump Courts Haley Stevens for GOP After She Rejects Abdul El-Sayed
text: Getting your Trinity Audio player ready… President Donald Trump wasted no time in courting Michigan Democrat Haley Stevens to change colors to the GOP on Sunday after the congresswoman endorsed Republican Mike Rogers for Senate over her former Democratic opponent Abdul El-Sayed. Steven’s defection to Rogers was roundly ridiculed among Democrats on Sunday, with prominent leaders like Chuck Schumer, Nancy Pelosi and Bernie Sanders all denouncing the congresswoman’s decision to reject El-Sayed as a betrayal to the party at large. Michigan’s Democratic Party Chair Curtis Hertel later announced that Stevens is no longer “a current member of the Michigan Democratic Party, nor will she be in the future.” The president told reporters Sunday that he called Stevens and thanked her for doing “the right thing” by endorsing his supporter Rogers, whom she previously criticized as a “rubber stamp for Donald Trump’s dangerous agenda.” “I’d love to have her,” Trump added when asked if he thinks she should join the Republican Party. The president then handed the spotlight to Speaker Mike Johnson, who said that he’d also sent Stevens a note of thanks for her action on Sunday. Q: Do you plan to reach out to Haley Stevens? Trump: Yes, to thank her. Q: Do you think she should be a member of the Republican Party? Trump: I’d love to have her. Johnson: I sent her a note. pic.twitter.com/dF3X4HTgxc — Acyn (@Acyn) November 1, 2026 “I sent her a note and told her how great she was and how much we appreciated that. She’s standing for truth,” Johnson said. “Haley is a good person, she’s always been very thoughtful, she loves her state, she’s served in it as best she could and she’s speaking the truth. This is a contest election between common sense and crazy, and there is no crazier choice on the ballot than El-Sayed, what he stands for, and he needs to answer for that.” Tensions have been mounting between El-Sayed and Stevens all week after the congresswoman called on the Democratic nominee to denounce an “antisemitic” ad that linked U.S. military aid to Israel and prices spiking in the grocery store. The ad came from an outside group, and El-Sayed said he disagreed with its message but criticized Stevens for “relitigating a primary that ended three months ago.” In the lead-up to a scheduled unity event on Sunday with Stevens, El-Sayed asked the congresswoman to stay away from future campaign events ahead of Tuesday’s midterms. “I would rather not distract from the key issues of this campaign,” he said Saturday. The rift between the two apparently irreparable, Stevens abandoned her support of the Democratic ticket and endorsed Republican opponent Rogers on Sunday, leading to widespread outcry from within her party and resignations from her longtime staff. “As you may have seen, our Democratic nominee for U.S. Senate, Abdul, said that I was no longer welcome in his campaign and that I should stay away. And he’s right, and that’s why I am endorsing Mike Rogers for the United States Senate today,” Stevens said in an Instagram video . “I don’t belong in Abdul’s campaign … I’m just letting you know where I am. I’m still a very proud Democrat. I still very much believe in everything I voted for and said, and I’ve worked really hard, and will continue to do so in all the ways life’s opportunities afford.” Responding to the about-face from his former Democratic opponent on Sunday, El-Sayed told press, simply , “None of this matters.” Read Next Haley Stevens Pulls Plug on Presser While Heckled as 'Traitor' for Endorsing Mike Rogers

title: Midterm elections live updates: 'We gave this a very strong shot,' Trump says in speech focused on his construction projects - ABC News
text: Live Midterm elections live updates: 'We gave this a very strong shot,' Trump says in speech focused on his construction projects Trump touted the newly reopened Reflecting Pool ahead of high-stakes midterms. 1:53 President Donald Trump delivers a speech marking the end of the midterm election campaign, in Washington, November 2, 2026. Evan Vucci/Reuters By ABC NEWS Last Updated: November 2, 2026, 4:43 PM EST The high-stakes midterm elections are a day away, and candidates are making their final pitches to voters. There are several key House and Senate races that could determine the balance of power in Congress as well as significant races for governor around the country. The elections could ultimately determine how effective President Donald Trump's agenda is in the back half of his second term. Key Headlines 1 hour and 6 minutes ago Trump's closing message: 'We gave this a very strong shot' 2 hours and 34 minutes ago Vance delivers closing midterm election remarks in Ohio 1:28 PM EST Justice Department asks SCOTUS to block CA from counting disputed ballots Here's how the news is developing. 13 Updates Nov 01, 2026, 6:44 PM EST Dem Rep. Stevens joins GOP candidate Rogers for press conference after surprise endorsement Michigan Democratic Rep. Haley Stevens and Republican Senate candidate Mike Rogers, in a joint press conference after Stevens endorsed Rogers, defended the decision as one that is right for Michigan, adding that it was about standing "with country." Stevens endorsed Rogers against Democratic nominee Dr. Abdul El-Sayed after Stevens had previously said she would support El-Sayed. Stevens said that “90% of the votes I'm going to cast are going to be for Democrats. My vote for Senate, I am just one vote, as is every Michigander. My vote for Senate is going to be with Mike Rogers. And I will tell you why. Because we have to stand with country." She said El-Sayed boxed her out of his campaign. "I did endorse the Democratic nominee, and he chose to close his campaign by saying I wasn't welcome… This is about looking in the mirror about how real Democrats for Rogers are." Nov 01, 2026, 2:13 PM EST Trump praises Democratic Rep. Haley Stevens for endorsing Republican Mike Rogers President Donald Trump lavished praise on Democratic Rep. Haley Stevens of Michigan after she endorsed Republican Mike Rogers on Sunday over Democrat Abdul El-Sayed in the Senate race, who defeated Stevens in the primary. “Wow, this is BIG!” Trump wrote on social media Sunday, reacting to the news. “Her following is huge, and the level of respect from the People of Michigan, especially our African American and Jewish populations, is virtually unparalleled. Haley said what few people are willing to say,” Trump further said, adding that Stevens showed “great and almost unprecedented loyalty” to Michigan. “It’s a thing called bravery, and few people have it like just displayed by Congresswoman Haley Stevens!” Trump said. -ABC News' Nicholas Kerr Nov 01, 2026, 1:55 PM EST Judge dismisses DOJ suit seeking to potentially block Alaska election results certification A federal judge on Sunday dismissed the Justice Department’s lawsuit seeking to block certification of the election in Alaska if the Democratic candidate for U.S. Senate wins, dealing yet another setback to the Trump administration as it seeks to impose itself on state-run elections just days before the midterm elections. The Justice Department filed the extraordinary lawsuit last week at the behest of President Donald Trump. Federal prosecutors requested a delay in the certification of the outcome to allow time to investigate whether confusion over two candidates with the same name, Dan Sullivan, could effect election results. U.S. Judge Sharon Gleason wrote in part that the Justice Department’s suit fails on the law, but also on the practicality of the request. “The United States provides no workable plan as to how it proposes to segregate ballots cast for Daniel J. Sullivan on Election Day and then conduct a court-ordered unspecified 'investigation’ of those ballots in a manner that would preserve voter secrecy,” Gleason wrote, referring to the Democratic candidate. The Justice Department told ABC News in a statement that it plans to appeal the ruling. -ABC News' Luc Bruggeman and Alex Mallin Nov 01, 2026, 12:59 PM EST Michigan Democratic Rep. Stevens endorses GOP Senate candidate Mike Rogers Michigan Democratic Rep. Haley Stevens on Sunday endorsed Republican Senate Candidate Mike Rogers. "I am endorsing Mike Rogers for the United States Senate," Stevens said in part in a video posted Sunday on X. Michigan Republican Senate candidate Mike Rogers, right, and Rep. Haley Stevens, D-Mich., attend a service at Perfecting Church, Nov. 1, 2026, in Detroit. Jose Juarez/AP Photo Stevens and Michigan Democratic Senate nominee Dr. Abdul El-Sayed, who defeated Stevens in the primary, have clashed in recent days over issues including a controversial campaign ad .
